categories.title: Sizing & hosting Blazor Server
categories.intro: Start here when the question is "how many nodes / how much memory / will it hold?"

links.label: Host and deploy server-side Blazor (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: The canonical starting point: circuit memory behaviour, scalability guidance, and load-balancer/affinity requirements. Read this before trusting any sizing rule of thumb.

links.label: ASP.NET Core Blazor SignalR guidance (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Circuit handler configuration, reconnect behaviour, and the knobs (DisconnectedCircuitMaxRetained, JSInterop timeouts) that directly drive the disconnected-circuit memory line in any capacity model.

links.label: Blazor Server threat mitigation & circuit lifecycle (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Reads as a security doc but doubles as the best description of resource exhaustion risks: per-circuit memory, connection limits, and denial-of-service surface.

links.label: Blazor Server Capacity Calculator (this site)
links.note: Our interactive model for nodes, SignalR units, memory, and message budget. Open source; the formulas are documented in the tool's glossary.

categories.title: Azure SignalR Service
categories.intro: Unit economics decide real cost at scale; connections and messages are both metered.

links.label: Azure SignalR Service performance guide (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Connection counts and message throughput per unit, with methodology. The numbers behind every 'connections per unit' assumption; verify against your tier before committing.

links.label: ASP.NET Core SignalR hosting and scaling (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: The decision doc for Azure SignalR Service vs. self-managed Redis backplane: sticky sessions, scale-out patterns, and their trade-offs.

links.label: Azure SignalR Service pricing
links.note: Included messages per unit per day by tier. SKU terms change; this page, not a blog post, is the source of truth for the message-budget inputs.

categories.title: Memory & diagnostics
categories.intro: You can't size what you haven't measured. These are the measurement tools.

links.label: .NET diagnostics tools overview (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Map of the whole dotnet-* diagnostics family (counters, trace, gcdump, dump) and when to reach for each.

links.label: dotnet-counters (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: First tool out of the bag in a soak test: live GC heap size, working set, and SignalR connection counters with zero profiler overhead.

links.label: dotnet-gcdump (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Heap snapshots you can diff: the practical way to attribute per-circuit memory cost and catch circuit-scoped leaks.

links.label: Garbage collection fundamentals (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Server GC vs. workstation GC and generation behaviour: context you need before interpreting any memory number on a Blazor Server node.

links.label: Memory management best practices for ASP.NET Core (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: The classic traps (captured HttpContext, unbounded caches, large object heap churn), most of which get amplified per-circuit in Blazor Server.

links.label: PerfView (GitHub)
links.note: Old UI, unmatched depth. When dotnet-counters says 'memory grows' and gcdump says 'somewhere in here', PerfView tells you exactly where.

links.label: David Fowler: ASP.NET Core Diagnostic Scenarios (GitHub)
links.note: Async and memory anti-patterns with corrected examples, from the ASP.NET architect. Many 'Blazor is slow' cases are actually one of these.

categories.title: Load & soak testing
categories.intro: A capacity plan is a hypothesis until a soak test confirms it.

links.label: crank: .NET benchmarking infrastructure (GitHub)
links.note: The load infrastructure the ASP.NET team itself uses for TechEmpower runs. Steeper setup than k6, but it speaks SignalR.

links.label: k6 (Grafana)
links.note: Scriptable load testing with WebSocket support. Good for driving realistic SignalR connection ramps; pair scenarios with dotnet-counters on the server side.

links.label: NBomber
links.note: Load testing in C#/F# that lets .NET teams write scenarios in the language they know, including against SignalR hubs with the real client library.

links.label: Azure Load Testing (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Managed option when you need geographic scale or CI/CD-integrated load gates without owning the injector fleet.

categories.title: .NET performance engineering
categories.intro: Broader .NET performance craft that pays off in every Blazor workload.

links.label: Stephen Toub: Performance improvements in .NET (annual series)
links.note: The annual deep-dive is the single best education in how .NET actually executes. Read the newest edition; skim earlier years for the cumulative picture.

links.label: BenchmarkDotNet (GitHub)
links.note: The standard for micro-benchmarks. Use it to settle 'is this render path/allocation pattern faster' arguments with data instead of opinion.

links.label: ASP.NET Core Blazor performance best practices (Microsoft Learn)
links.note: Component-level rendering optimizations: virtualization, ShouldRender, event throttling. This is the per-circuit CPU/allocation side of the scaling story.

categories.title: Community
categories.intro: Where Blazor practitioners actually compare notes.

links.label: Awesome Blazor (GitHub)
links.note: The community's index of Blazor libraries, tools, and articles. Broad rather than performance-focused, but the standard first stop.

links.label: .NET Community Standups
links.note: The ASP.NET/Blazor standups are where roadmap and performance work get discussed months before documentation lands.

links.label: .NET Blog: ASP.NET Core & Blazor posts
links.note: Release-cycle posts routinely include Blazor scalability changes (rendering modes, SignalR improvements) worth folding into capacity assumptions.
